justification: These ranges describe what a typical low-stakes full-ring limit opponent holds after each preflop line, before we have watched them play. With eight to ten players at the table, someone behind is more likely to hold a big hand, so every seat plays tighter than at six-handed. Typical players raise less often than a solid chart suggests and limp with part of the rest, especially small pairs and suited hands that like a cheap multiway flop. Re-raises from the early seats are almost always big pairs or ace with king. The big blind still checks or defends with many hands because it already has a bet in the pot. After the flop the narrowing rule trims each starting range street by street from what the player does.

ranges.justification: In an unraised full-ring pot the big blind checks with every hand it chose not to raise, so only its better pairs and strongest aces are missing from this very wide range.
